readerQuestion: Which doorbell should I buy for Home Assistant, and what extra hardware, app choices and feature limits do I need to check?
directAnswer: Start with powered Reolink for a new local setup, compare UniFi when Protect is already installed, and compare Aqara G400 Wired or G410 for Apple Home. Verify video, button events, recordings and talk separately. Battery operation does not imply cloud dependence, but it changes streaming expectations and may require a hub.
originalContribution: The four-function checklist distinguishes a usable front-door workflow from a camera compatibility badge. The one-door worked purchase plan compares incremental hardware costs for an Ethernet-capable home, an existing Protect installation and a no-wiring home. The acceptance checks cover real button presses, repeat alerts, clip retrieval, actual phone talk, local-only operation and battery sleep without using lock or alarm actions.
limitations: Documentation research and website tests, not hands-on doorbell testing. No measured talk latency, image quality, battery duration, availability, price, or Home Assistant hardware compatibility is claimed. G6 and Aqara video/bridge specifications do not establish every Home Assistant event or access-control feature. Source image is Reolink manufacturer imagery, not a Tara installation photograph. More useful content and successful deployment do not prove ranking recovery.

claimChecks.claim: Powered Reolink has a local integration with visitor signals; battery doorbells use a compatible hub/NVR and viewing can keep them awake.
White and black PoE variants have different framing and package-detection specifications.
The specified Reolink PoE/Wi-Fi models can reuse suitable power wiring but do not ring an existing mechanical chime.
UniFi full-access mode and limited API-key-only mode expose different domains; API-key-only currently lacks events.
G6 Entry specifies Protect/Access and PoE+ power, not a normal low-voltage doorbell transformer.
G6 Pro Entry likewise specifies PoE+ and Protect/Access.
TP-Link lists D130 and D230, with device-account prerequisites and live view conditional on support.
D230 lacks general RTSP support; D225/D235/TD25 require specified hardwiring, jumper and always-on configuration for RTSP.
G400 supports PoE/low-voltage power and RTSP/ONVIF, does not use a traditional chime, and requires a card for continuous recording/NAS backup.
G410's RTSP and continuous recording require wired power; advertised Matter bridging is distinct from a camera feed.
HomeKit Secure Video stores encrypted clips in iCloud and requires the corresponding iCloud+ and home-hub setup.
Ring supports live view and real-time events while polling status; last recording needs a subscription and live-view two-way talk is excluded.
HomeKit Bridge exports Home Assistant entities to Apple Home; it is not an arbitrary camera-import integration.
